summary: Washington County, Maine: 1918 enclosed wooden lookout, replaced by a 70-foot steel tower in 1934; cut down by new owners in 2007.

facts.design: Enclosed wooden tower, 55 ft, built 1918; replaced in 1934 by a 70-ft steel tower
facts.status_note: Cut down and dropped by new landowners in summer 2007; watchman cabin removed early 2008

events.note: New landowners cut the tower down and dropped it; the new owners did not want to deal with it
Watchman cabin removed by the new landowners in early 2008

evidence.supports: Built in 1918 as an enclosed wooden tower, 55 feet high; replaced in 1934 by a 70-foot steel tower
evidence.quote: The Forest Service fire lookout tower on Washington Bald Mountain, built in 1918, was the older, enclosed wood type. It was 55-feet high and was replaced in 1934 with a 70-foot steel tower.

evidence.supports: The mountain is in Township 42 MD
evidence.quote: Washington Bald in T42 MD was cut down and dropped by the new landowners this past summer.

evidence.supports: The mountain is in Washington County; listed as gone
evidence.quote: Washington Bald Mountain Washington 45.09818 -67.92316 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Summer 2007: new landowners cut the tower down and dropped it
evidence.quote: Washington Bald in T42 MD was cut down and dropped by the new landowners this past summer.

evidence.supports: New owners, Sustainable Forest Technologies of Milford, were not willing to take on the tower
evidence.quote: The new owners, Sustainable Forest Technologies of Milford did not want to deal with the tower.

evidence.supports: Watchman cabin removed by the new landowners in early 2008
evidence.quote: its watchman cabin was removed by the new landowners in early 2008.

sources.title: Washington Bald Mountain fire lookout tower, ca. 1920

notes_for_editor: The 2007 report does not say whether the tower cut down was the 1918 wood tower or the 1934 steel tower; the story says only 'the tower'. Brief event wording matches the 2007 report. No staffing source found. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not read. No source read describes the site today or public access.
